observed_steps.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}25 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ -5 & 25\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}26 & 130 \\ 130 & -598\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & -23\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-24,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}25 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ -5 & 25\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}26 & 130 \\ 130 & -598\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & -23\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

observed_steps.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A = \lambda_1 \mathbf u_1\cdot \mathbf u_1^T + \lambda_2 \mathbf u_2\cdot \mathbf u_2^T,
$$

where $\mathbf u_1$ and $\mathbf u_2$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2,$ respectively.

Moreover, $\mathbf u_i\cdot \mathbf u_i^T$ is the projection matrix corresponding to $\mathbf u_i.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda=-1.$ Computing $A-(-1)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain $x_1=\dfrac12x_2.$ Hence, the general solution is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155034/assets/a9be58f43f2f6487ef226b7e8d4e8622bcd352978dcb525c235382a27769f21f.svg)

Therefore, setting $x_2=2,$ we get the eigenvector 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155034/assets/8500837975640706a5da0ecfe0bdd2058b5707e834a662172a82482105cda068.svg)

where $\| \mathbf{v} \| = \sqrt{5}.$ Dividing $\mathbf{v}$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155034/assets/0f6d44b312837955c0dd6e842219ed995297db12bdf0d46240a874205ab948a9.svg)

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

observed_steps.name: Question 11
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Finding a Projection Matrix That Orthogonally Projects a Vector to the Subspace Spanned by an Eigenvector

observed_steps.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =2.$ Computing $A-2I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{2}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem: Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps $x\in {R}^{2}$ onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].$

Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps x∈R2 onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue λ=2 of the matrix A=[5335].

EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

Moreover, ui⋅uiT is the projection matrix corresponding to ui.

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to λ=2. Computing A−2I, we get

A−2I=[5335]−2[1001]=[3333].

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[330330]R2:=R2+(−1)R1∼[330000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=−x2. Hence, the general solution is

[−x2x2],x2∈R.

Therefore, setting x2=1, we get the eigenvector

v=[−11],

where ‖v‖=2. Dividing v by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: u=v‖v‖=12[−11]

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

u⋅uT=12[−11]⋅12[−11]=12[−11]⋅[−11]=12[1−1−11].

The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =2.$ Computing $A-2I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 18\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -4 & 16\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -4 & 16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 0 \\ -4 & 16 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=4{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{17}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{17}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{17}[\begin{aligned}16 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps x∈R2 onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue λ=2 of the matrix A=[3−4−418].

a
117[16441]
b
117[1−4−416]
c
117[1−4−416]
d
17[16441]
e
117[16441]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

Moreover, ui⋅uiT is the projection matrix corresponding to ui.

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to λ=2. Computing A−2I, we get

A−2I=[3−4−418]−2[1−4−416]=[1−4−416].

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[1−40−4160]R2:=R2+4R1∼[1−40000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=4x2. Hence, the general solution is

[4x2x2],x2∈R.

Therefore, setting x2=1, we get the eigenvector

v=[41],

where ‖v‖=17. Dividing v by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: u=v‖v‖=117[41]

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

u⋅uT=117[41]⋅117[41]=117[41]⋅[41]=117[16441].

observed_steps.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =-1.$ Computing $A-(-1)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A+I & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 6 \\ 6 & 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & 0 \\ 6 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{13}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{13}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{13}[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -6 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13

Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps x∈R2 onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue λ=−1 of the matrix A=[8663].

a
113[4−6−69]
b
113[9664]
c
113[4−6−69]
d
113[−944−6]
e
13[9664]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

Moreover, ui⋅uiT is the projection matrix corresponding to ui.

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to λ=−1. Computing A−(−1)I, we get

A+I=[8663]+[1001]=[9664].

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[960640]R2:=R2+(−23)R1∼[960000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=−23x2. Hence, the general solution is

[−23x2x2],x2∈R.

Therefore, setting x2=3, we get the eigenvector

v=[−23],

where ‖v‖=13. Dividing v by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: u=v‖v‖=113[−23]

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

u⋅uT=113[−23]⋅113[−23]=113[−23]⋅[−23]=113[4−6−69].

observed_steps.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =5.$ Computing $A-5I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{5}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps x∈R2 onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue λ=5 of the matrix A=[1224].

a
15[1224]
b
15[1224]
c
15[−4−1−12]
d
[4221]
e
15[4221]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

Moreover, ui⋅uiT is the projection matrix corresponding to ui.

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to λ=5. Computing A−5I, we get

A−5I=[1224]−5[1001]=[−422−1].

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[−420210]R2:=R2+12R1∼[−420000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=12x2. Hence, the general solution is

[12x2x2],x2∈R.

Therefore, setting x2=2, we get the eigenvector

v=[12],

where ‖v‖=5. Dividing v by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: u=v‖v‖=15[12]

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

u⋅uT=15[12]⋅15[12]=15[12]⋅[12]=15[1224].

The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =8.$ Computing $A-8I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-8I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -5 \\ -5 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & -5 & 0 \\ -5 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{2}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

Moreover, ui⋅uiT is the projection matrix corresponding to ui.

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to λ=8. Computing A−8I, we get

A−8I=[3−5−53]−8[1001]=[−5−5−5−5].

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[−5−50−5−50]R2:=R2+(−1)R1∼[−5−50000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=−x2. Hence, the general solution is

[−x2x2],x2∈R.

Therefore, setting x2=1, we get the eigenvector

where ‖v‖=2. Dividing v by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: u=v‖v‖=12[−11]

question.name: Question 1
question.problem:
Given that $A$ is a $5\times 5$ real symmetric matrix, which of the following statements are true?

I. $A$ must have $5$ distinct eigenvalues

II. $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable

III. If $u$ and $v$ are two eigenvectors that correspond to the same eigenvalue, then $u⊥v$
question.worked_solution:
Given that $A$ is an $n\times n$ symmetric matrix over $R$, the spectral theorem states the following:

- The eigenvalues of $A$ are all real.

- Eigenvectors corresponding to different eigenvalues are orthogonal.

- The dimension of the eigenspace for each eigenvalue equals the multiplicity of that eigenvalue as a root of the characteristic polynomial.

- $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is false. According to the spectral theorem, the eigenvalues are real but not necessarily distinct. This occurs when the characteristic polynomial has roots whose (algebraic) multiplicity is greater than $1.$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, any symmetric matrix with real entries is orthogonally diagonalizable.

- Statement III is false. According to the theorem, eigenvectors corresponding to different eigenvalues must be orthogonal, but two eigenvectors that correspond to the same eigenvalue may not be orthogonal.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

  • Statement III is false. According to the theorem, any symmetric matrix with real entries is orthogonally diagonalizable, but not necessarily orthogonal.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

question.name: Question 5
question.problem:
Given that $A$ is a real symmetric matrix, which of the following statements are true?

I. $A$ must have all real eigenvalues

II. $A$ is diagonalizable

III. If $u$ and $v$ are two eigenvectors that correspond to different eigenvalues, then $u=\alpha v$ for some scalar $\alpha $
question.worked_solution:
Given that $A$ is an $n\times n$ symmetric matrix over $R$, the spectral theorem states the following:

- The eigenvalues of $A$ are all real.

- Eigenvectors corresponding to different eigenvalues are orthogonal.

- The dimension of the eigenspace for each eigenvalue equals the multiplicity of that eigenvalue as a root of the characteristic polynomial.

- $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement III is true. Indeed, the eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix are real.

- Statement II is true. Indeed, any symmetric matrix with real entries is orthogonally diagonalizable, hence, is diagonalizable.

- Statement I is false. According to the spectral theorem, eigenvectors corresponding to different eigenvalues must be orthogonal. Since the eigenvector are nonzero, we can't have $u=\alpha v$ for some scalar $\alpha .$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

question.name: Question 6
question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=8,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}10 & 6 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}10 & 6 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=8,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}10 & 6 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 6
?

Suppose that

v1=[−11] and v2=[11]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=2 and λ2=8, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[2112]
b
[−3−5−5−3]
c
[106610]
d
[2332]
e
[5335]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=12[−11]u2=v2‖v2‖=12[11]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=2⋅12[−11]⋅12[−11]+8⋅12[11]⋅12[11]=2⋅12[−11][−11]+8⋅12[11][11]=12(2⋅[−11][−11]+8⋅[11][11])=12(2⋅[1−1−11]+8⋅[1111])=12[106610]=[5335].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Spectral Decomposition of a Symmetric Matrix

solution.reasoning: The eigenvectors are orthogonal and each has squared norm 2. Spectral decomposition gives A=(2/2)v₁v₁ᵀ+(8/2)v₂v₂ᵀ=[[1,-1],[-1,1]]+4[[1,1],[1,1]]=[[5,3],[3,5]]. Verification: A(-1,1)ᵀ=(-2,2)ᵀ and A(1,1)ᵀ=(8,8)ᵀ. Thus option e is mathematically correct. The captured worked solution concerns a different matrix and supplies no Math Academy answer evidence for this current question.

feedback.name: Question 6
feedback.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=8,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]+8\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}10 & 6 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6

Suppose that

v1=[−11] and v2=[11]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=2 and λ2=8, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[2112]
b
[−3−5−5−3]
c
[106610]
d
[2332]
e
[5335]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=12[−11]u2=v2‖v2‖=12[11]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=2⋅12[−11]⋅12[−11]+8⋅12[11]⋅12[11]=2⋅12[−11][−11]+8⋅12[11][11]=12(2⋅[−11][−11]+8⋅[11][11])=12(2⋅[1−1−11]+8⋅[1111])=12[106610]=[5335].

question.name: Question 7
question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 7
?

Suppose that

v1=[11] and v2=[1−1]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=−1 and λ2=1, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[0−2−20]
b
[1221]
c
[0−1−10]
d
[2112]
e
[1−1−11]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=12[11]u2=v2‖v2‖=12[1−1]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=(−1)⋅12[11]⋅12[11]+1⋅12[1−1]⋅12[1−1]=(−1)⋅12[11][11]+1⋅12[1−1][1−1]=12((−1)⋅[11][11]+1⋅[1−1][1−1])=12((−1)⋅[1111]+1⋅[1−1−11])=12[0−2−20]=[0−1−10].

last_observation.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 7
question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 7
?

Suppose that

v1=[11] and v2=[1−1]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=−1 and λ2=1, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[0−2−20]
b
[1221]
c
[0−1−10]
d
[2112]
e
[1−1−11]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=12[11]u2=v2‖v2‖=12[1−1]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=(−1)⋅12[11]⋅12[11]+1⋅12[1−1]⋅12[1−1]=(−1)⋅12[11][11]+1⋅12[1−1][1−1]=12((−1)⋅[11][11]+1⋅[1−1][1−1])=12((−1)⋅[1111]+1⋅[1−1−11])=12[0−2−20]=[0−1−10].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Spectral Decomposition of a Symmetric Matrix

solution.reasoning: The eigenvectors are orthogonal and each has squared norm 2. Thus A=−(1/2)v₁v₁ᵀ+(1/2)v₂v₂ᵀ=[[0,−1],[−1,0]]. This matrix sends (1,1)ᵀ to (−1,−1)ᵀ and (1,−1)ᵀ to (1,−1)ᵀ, giving the required eigenvalues −1 and 1. Option c is mathematically correct. The captured worked example solves a different question, so Math Academy's current answer key is not established.

feedback.name: Question 7
feedback.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(-1)\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Suppose that

v1=[11] and v2=[1−1]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=−1 and λ2=1, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[0−2−20]
b
[1221]
c
[0−1−10]
d
[2112]
e
[1−1−11]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=12[11]u2=v2‖v2‖=12[1−1]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=(−1)⋅12[11]⋅12[11]+1⋅12[1−1]⋅12[1−1]=(−1)⋅12[11][11]+1⋅12[1−1][1−1]=12((−1)⋅[11][11]+1⋅[1−1][1−1])=12((−1)⋅[1111]+1⋅[1−1−11])=12[0−2−20]=[0−1−10].

question.name: Question 8
question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-5,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 \\ -8 & 16\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}15 & 20 \\ 20 & -15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Suppose that

v1=[21] and v2=[−24]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=5 and λ2=−5, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[3−2−2−3]
b
[344−3]
c
[2−2−2−2]
d
[422−5]
e
[3443]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=15[21]u2=v2‖v2‖=125[−24]

Therefore, we have

last_observation.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 \\ -8 & 16\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}15 & 20 \\ 20 & -15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-5,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 \\ -8 & 16\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}15 & 20 \\ 20 & -15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 8
?

Suppose that

v1=[21] and v2=[−24]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=5 and λ2=−5, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[3−2−2−3]
b
[344−3]
c
[2−2−2−2]
d
[422−5]
e
[3443]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=15[21]u2=v2‖v2‖=125[−24]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=5⋅15[21]⋅15[21]+(−5)⋅125[−24]⋅125[−24]=5⋅15[21][21]+(−5)⋅120[−24][−24]=15(5⋅[21][21]+(−5)⋅14[−24][−24])=15(5⋅[4221]+(−5)⋅14[4−8−816])=15(5⋅[4221]+(−5)⋅[1−2−24])=15[152020−15]=[344−3].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Spectral Decomposition of a Symmetric Matrix

solution.reasoning: The eigenvectors are orthogonal, with squared norms 5 and 20. Spectral decomposition gives A=(5/5)v₁v₁ᵀ−(5/20)v₂v₂ᵀ=[[4,2],[2,1]]−[[1,−2],[−2,4]]=[[3,4],[4,−3]]. Verification gives Av₁=(10,5)ᵀ=5v₁ and Av₂=(10,−20)ᵀ=−5v₂. Thus option b is mathematically correct. The captured example solves a different question and does not establish Math Academy's current answer key.

feedback.name: Question 8
feedback.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-5,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 4\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 \\ -8 & 16\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}15 & 20 \\ 20 & -15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8

Suppose that

v1=[21] and v2=[−24]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=5 and λ2=−5, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[3−2−2−3]
b
[344−3]
c
[2−2−2−2]
d
[422−5]
e
[3443]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=15[21]u2=v2‖v2‖=125[−24]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=5⋅15[21]⋅15[21]+(−5)⋅125[−24]⋅125[−24]=5⋅15[21][21]+(−5)⋅120[−24][−24]=15(5⋅[21][21]+(−5)⋅14[−24][−24])=15(5⋅[4221]+(−5)⋅14[4−8−816])=15(5⋅[4221]+(−5)⋅[1−2−24])=15[152020−15]=[344−3].

question.name: Question 9
question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-24,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}25 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ -5 & 25\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}26 & 130 \\ 130 & -598\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & -23\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

a
[155−23]

[255−21]

u1=v1‖v1‖=126[51]u2=v2‖v2‖=126[1−5]

last_observation.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}25 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ -5 & 25\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}26 & 130 \\ 130 & -598\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & -23\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-24,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}25 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ -5 & 25\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}26 & 130 \\ 130 & -598\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & -23\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 9
?

Suppose that

v1=[51] and v2=[1−5]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=2 and λ2=−24, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[155−23]
b
[155−17]
c
[255−21]
d
[144−18]
e
[244−17]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=126[51]u2=v2‖v2‖=126[1−5]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=2⋅126[51]⋅126[51]+(−24)⋅126[1−5]⋅126[1−5]=2⋅126[51][51]+(−24)⋅126[1−5][1−5]=126(2⋅[51][51]+(−24)⋅[1−5][1−5])=126(2⋅[25551]+(−24)⋅[1−5−525])=126[26130130−598]=[155−23].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Spectral Decomposition of a Symmetric Matrix

solution.reasoning: The eigenvectors are orthogonal and each has squared norm 26. Spectral decomposition gives A=(2/26)[[25,5],[5,1]]−(24/26)[[1,−5],[−5,25]]=[[1,5],[5,−23]]. Verification: A(5,1)ᵀ=(10,2)ᵀ=2(5,1)ᵀ and A(1,−5)ᵀ=(−24,120)ᵀ=−24(1,−5)ᵀ. Thus option a is mathematically correct. The supplied worked example answers a different question, so Math Academy's current key is not captured.

feedback.name: Question 9
feedback.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-24,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot \frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}(2\cdot [\begin{aligned}25 & 5 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]+(-24)\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ -5 & 25\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}26 & 130 \\ 130 & -598\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & -23\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=2 and λ2=−24, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[155−23]

[155−17]

[255−21]

[144−18]

EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

u1=v1‖v1‖=126[51]u2=v2‖v2‖=126[1−5]

question.name: Question 10
question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=13$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-12,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =13\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =13\cdot \frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot \frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}(13\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}(13\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 & -12 \\ -12 & 16\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot [\begin{aligned}16 & 12 \\ 12 & 9\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}-75 & -300 \\ -300 & 100\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -12 \\ -12 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Suppose that

v1=[−34] and v2=[43]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=13 and λ2=−12, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[9−10−1011]
b
[5−15−1510]
c
[89915]
d
[−3−12−124]
e
[6141418]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=15[−34]u2=v2‖v2‖=15[43]

Therefore, we have

last_observation.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =13\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =13\cdot \frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot \frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}(13\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}(13\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 & -12 \\ -12 & 16\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot [\begin{aligned}16 & 12 \\ 12 & 9\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}-75 & -300 \\ -300 & 100\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -12 \\ -12 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 10
question.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=13$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-12,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =13\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =13\cdot \frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot \frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}(13\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}(13\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 & -12 \\ -12 & 16\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot [\begin{aligned}16 & 12 \\ 12 & 9\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}-75 & -300 \\ -300 & 100\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -12 \\ -12 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 10
?

Suppose that

v1=[−34] and v2=[43]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=13 and λ2=−12, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[9−10−1011]
b
[5−15−1510]
c
[89915]
d
[−3−12−124]
e
[6141418]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=15[−34]u2=v2‖v2‖=15[43]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=13⋅15[−34]⋅15[−34]+(−12)⋅15[43]⋅15[43]=13⋅125[−34][−34]+(−12)⋅125[43][43]=125(13⋅[−34][−34]+(−12)⋅[43][43])=125(13⋅[9−12−1216]+(−12)⋅[1612129])=125[−75−300−300100]=[−3−12−124].
question.knowledge_point: Finding the Spectral Decomposition of a Symmetric Matrix

solution.reasoning: The eigenvectors are orthogonal and each has squared norm 25. Spectral decomposition gives A=(13/25)[[9,−12],[−12,16]]−(12/25)[[16,12],[12,9]]=[[−3,−12],[−12,4]]. Verification: A(−3,4)ᵀ=(−39,52)ᵀ=13(−3,4)ᵀ and A(4,3)ᵀ=(−48,−36)ᵀ=−12(4,3)ᵀ. Thus option d is mathematically correct. The captured worked example concerns a different question and does not establish Math Academy's current answer key.

feedback.name: Question 10
feedback.problem:
Suppose that

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$

are eigenvectors of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=13$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-12,$ respectively. Find the matrix $A.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\  & =13\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =13\cdot \frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot \frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}(13\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 4\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 3\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}(13\cdot [\begin{aligned}9 & -12 \\ -12 & 16\end{aligned}]+(-12)\cdot [\begin{aligned}16 & 12 \\ 12 & 9\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}-75 & -300 \\ -300 & 100\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -12 \\ -12 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Suppose that

v1=[−34] and v2=[43]

are eigenvectors of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A that correspond to the eigenvalues λ1=13 and λ2=−12, respectively. Find the matrix A.

a
[9−10−1011]
b
[5−15−1510]
c
[89915]
d
[−3−12−124]
e
[6141418]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

u1=v1‖v1‖=15[−34]u2=v2‖v2‖=15[43]

Therefore, we have

A=λ1u1u1T+λ2u2u2T=13⋅15[−34]⋅15[−34]+(−12)⋅15[43]⋅15[43]=13⋅125[−34][−34]+(−12)⋅125[43][43]=125(13⋅[−34][−34]+(−12)⋅[43][43])=125(13⋅[9−12−1216]+(−12)⋅[1612129])=125[−75−300−300100]=[−3−12−124].

question.name: Question 11
question.problem: Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps $x\in {R}^{2}$ onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =2.$ Computing $A-2I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{2}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11

Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps x∈R2 onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue λ=2 of the matrix A=[5335].

a
13[2332]
b
12[1−1−11]
c
12[1221]
d
13[3−2−23]
e
[1111]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

Moreover, ui⋅uiT is the projection matrix corresponding to ui.

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to λ=2. Computing A−2I, we get

A−2I=[5335]−2[1001]=[3333].

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[330330]R2:=R2+(−1)R1∼[330000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=−x2. Hence, the general solution is

[−x2x2],x2∈R.

Therefore, setting x2=1, we get the eigenvector

v=[−11],

where ‖v‖=2. Dividing v by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: u=v‖v‖=12[−11]

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

u⋅uT=12[−11]⋅12[−11]=12[−11]⋅[−11]=12[1−1−11].

The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =2.$ Computing $A-2I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{2}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
